paper.title: Performance Comparison of Different Machine Learning Techniques for Early Prediction of Breast Cancer using Wisconsin Breast Cancer Dataset
paper.venue: 2022 3rd International Informatics and Software Engineering Conference (IISEC)

task.problem_type: Binary classification of breast cancer cases into benign vs malignant
task.goal: Compare ANN, SVM, and Random Forest for early breast cancer prediction on the Wisconsin Breast Cancer dataset

dataset.name: Wisconsin Breast Cancer Dataset
dataset.replication_note: The paper is internally inconsistent. Page 3 says the dataset has 699 instances and 11 attributes, while page 4 says 'Out of the 569 examples, we used 398 for the training set and 171 for testing.' The feature table on page 3 lists only 9 named features.

reported_steps: categorical data conversion into numerical data
preprocessing.implementation_note: The paper states StandardScaler with fit_transform() was used to compress large and very small values into a certain range.
missing_or_unclear_details: Whether duplicates were actually present and removed
Which columns were categorical and how they were encoded
Whether the train/test split was stratified
Whether scaling was fit on training only or the full dataset

ANN.other_parameters_note: The paper says 'and these other parameters' but does not specify them.

cross_validation.description: Dataset separated into 10 chunks; 9 folds used for training and 1 fold used for analysis/testing

evaluation_protocol.metric_definition_note: The formulas table appears inconsistent: it defines precision as TP/(TP+TN), which is not the standard precision formula. This is likely a paper error.

results.paper_conclusion: ANN achieved the highest prediction performance among the three algorithms.

minimum_reproducible_setup_from_paper: Use the Wisconsin Breast Cancer dataset from UCI.
Standardize features with sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler using fit_transform().
Train and compare ANN, SVM, and Random Forest.
Use SVM with kernel='rbf' and degree=3.
Use ANN with ReLU in dense layers, sigmoid in the last layer, Sparse Categorical Cross Entropy loss, RMSprop optimizer, batch size 1, and 10 epochs.
Use Random Forest with n_estimators=100 and criterion='gini'.
Evaluate using 10-fold cross-validation and report accuracy, AUC, precision, recall, and F-score.
replication_gaps: Dataset size is inconsistently reported as both 699 and 569.
Train/test split description conflicts with the 10-fold CV description.
Critical SVM and Random Forest hyperparameters are missing.
No seed or implementation code is provided.
replication_takeaways.replication_risk: High, due to multiple inconsistencies and missing implementation details.
